name: Paraiso rectocele repair
question: How do posterior colporrhaphy, site-specific rectocele repair, and porcine-graft-augmented site-specific repair compare for posterior vaginal wall prolapse?

design.blinding: Patients blinded immediately after surgery; postoperative assessments by a blinded nurse; surgeons not blinded

arms.label: site-specific rectocele repair with porcine small-intestinal-submucosa graft

design.population: 106 women at least 21 years old with stage II or greater posterior vaginal wall prolapse; concomitant prolapse or incontinence surgery was permitted.
design.locator: Full text, Material and methods, pp 1763-1764

verdictNote: Fortagen graft augmentation had the lowest one-year anatomic cure rate.
takeaway: In 106 women randomized to posterior colporrhaphy, site-specific repair, or Fortagen graft-augmented site-specific repair, one-year anatomic cure was 24/28, 21/27, and 14/26, respectively (P = .02); patient-reported outcomes did not differ among groups.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Paraiso MFR, Barber MD, Muir TW, Walters MD. "Rectocele repair: a randomized trial of three surgical techniques including graft augmentation." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2006;195(6):1762-1771. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2006.07.026
reports.followUp: One-year anatomic assessment; 98/105 operated participants returned (mean follow-up 17.5 ± 7 months)
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Abstract, p 1762; Results, p 1764

results.note: Pearson chi-square three-group comparison among 81 assessed at one year; analyzed by randomized assignment.
results.locator: Full text, Material and methods, p 1764; Results, p 1765

results.measure: One-year PFDI-20 and PFIQ-7 total scores, mean ± SD

effect.p: <0.001 within each group; 0.28 PFDI-20 and 0.65 PFIQ-7 between groups

results.note: Prolapse, colorectal, urinary, and summary scales improved within all groups without between-group differences.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 1765; Table V, p 1769

results.measure: Worsening POPDI-6 and/or CRADI-8 score at one year
results.note: 15/88 (17%) among participants with one-year functional assessments; no significant between-group difference.
results.locator: Full text, Table I, p 1765; Results, p 1765

results.note: Improved in all groups without between-group differences.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 1766; Table VI, p 1769

results.endpoint: Posterior prolapse to or beyond the hymen
results.measure: POP-Q point Bp ≥ 0 at one year
results.note: The three-group difference was not statistically significant.
results.locator: Full text, Table I and Results, p 1765

results.measure: Bothersome splinting at one year, adjusted for treatment group and baseline symptoms
results.note: 82/105 operated participants underwent perineorrhaphy; this was an association across randomized groups, not a randomized comparison of perineorrhaphy.

harms.label: Dyspareunia

values.pc: 4/20 usually or always at one year
values.ss: 3/22 usually or always at one year
values.graft: 1/19 usually or always at one year

harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 1766; Table VI, p 1769
harms.note: No significant within-group change or between-group difference in dyspareunia distribution (between-group P = .45).

harms.label: Postoperative infection
harms.note: Within six weeks of surgery; UTI P = .54 and infection requiring antibiotics P = .13. Categories may overlap.

harms.label: Reoperation

values.pc: Prolapse reoperation 1/33; early return to operating room 0/37
values.ss: Prolapse reoperation 2/37; early return to operating room 0/37
values.graft: Prolapse reoperation 3/29; early return to operating room 1/31

harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 1765; Table IV, p 1768
harms.note: Prolapse reoperations involved any segment during the study (P = .47); one graft-arm patient returned to surgery on the operative day for bleeding.

harms.label: Graft exposure
harms.value: No graft exposures or graft complications were reported among 31 operated women assigned to the graft arm; one received SurgiSIS instead of Fortagen.

delivery.label: Operation received and operative time
delivery.value: 105/106 randomized participants underwent surgery; three protocol violations were analyzed by original assignment.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 1764; Table IV, p 1768
delivery.note: Mean ± SD operating time; between-group P = .61. All but four operated participants had concomitant procedures.

delivery.label: Assessment schedule
delivery.value: Postoperative visits at six weeks, six months, one year, and two years; blinded nurse performed POP-Q and questionnaire assessments at six months, one year, and two years.
delivery.locator: Full text, Material and methods, p 1764

delivery.label: Repair techniques and graft material
delivery.value: Posterior colporrhaphy plicated rectovaginal fibromuscularis without levator plication; site-specific repair reapproximated discrete defects. The graft arm added a 4 × 8 cm Fortagen porcine small-intestinal-submucosa graft (Organogenesis), perforated in three to four rows of 3-mm incisions and fixed superiorly to posterior vaginal fibromuscularis and epithelium, laterally to levator ani fascia, and inferiorly to perineal body.
delivery.locator: Full text, Material and methods, pp 1763-1764
